name: English Language
topics: Oral English: consonant sounds and clusters
Oral English: emphatic stress and intonation
Comprehension: a short original passage written into the question

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'The headmaster was COMMENDED for his excellent leadership during the school's anniversary.'
questions.e: To be COMMENDED means to be praised or spoken well of for doing something good. The headmaster was praised for his good leadership, so 'praised' fits best.
questions.p: COMMENDED mean say dem praise you for something good wey you do. Dem praise the headmaster because e lead well, so 'praised' na the correct answer.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'Chidi's ABUNDANT wealth did not change his simple lifestyle.'
questions.e: ABUNDANT means existing in large quantity, that is, plentiful. Chidi had a lot of wealth, so 'plentiful' is the correct synonym.
questions.p: ABUNDANT mean say e plenty well well. Chidi get plenty money, so 'plentiful' na the correct word wey mean the same thing.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'The old bridge was so FRAGILE that the council banned heavy vehicles from using it.'
questions.e: FRAGILE means easily broken or weak, hence 'delicate'. The bridge could easily collapse, which is why heavy vehicles were banned, so the sentence supports weakness, not strength.
questions.p: FRAGILE mean say e fit break quick quick, na weak thing. Na why dem ban heavy motor from the bridge, so 'delicate' na the correct answer, no be 'strong'.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'Many villagers felt RELUCTANT to leave their ancestral home despite the flood warning.'
questions.e: RELUCTANT means unwilling or hesitant to do something. The villagers did not want to leave their home even with the flood warning, so 'unwilling' fits perfectly.
questions.p: RELUCTANT mean say person no won do something, e dey hesitate. The villagers no won leave their house even with the flood warning, so 'unwilling' na the correct answer.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'The governor's speech was full of AMBIGUOUS statements that confused many listeners.'
questions.e: AMBIGUOUS means having more than one possible meaning, which causes confusion, so it is close to 'unclear'. The sentence says the statements confused listeners, confirming that they were not clear.
questions.p: AMBIGUOUS mean say the thing fit mean plenty different way, e dey confuse person. Since e confuse the listeners, the correct word na 'unclear', no be 'clear'.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'Mrs. Okafor's BLUNT comments during the meeting embarrassed some staff members.'
questions.e: In this context, BLUNT does not mean 'not sharp'; it means speaking in a very straightforward, plain way without softening the message. This directness is what embarrassed the staff, so 'direct' is the best synonym here.
questions.p: For this sentence, BLUNT no mean 'no sharp', e mean say person talk true-true without softening am. Na why the comment embarrass the staff, so 'direct' na the correct answer.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the word in CAPITALS.

'The journalist's CANDID report revealed the truth about the company's failures.'
questions.e: CANDID means truthful and straightforward, especially when the truth may be unpleasant. Since the report revealed the real truth about the company's failures, 'honest' is the closest meaning, not 'biased' or 'secret'.
questions.p: CANDID mean say person talk true thing even if e no sweet. Since the report show the real truth about the company wahala, 'honest' na the correct word, no be 'biased' or 'secret'.

questions.q:
Which of the options is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals?

GENEROUS
questions.e: Generous means willing to give freely to others. Stingy means unwilling to give or spend, so it is the direct opposite.
questions.p: Generous mean say person like give freely. Stingy mean say person no wan give at all, so na the opposite.

questions.q:
Which of the options is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals?

ANCIENT
questions.e: Ancient means very old or belonging to a long time ago. Modern means belonging to present times, which is the exact opposite.
questions.p: Ancient mean say something old well-well from long time. Modern mean say e dey happen now, so na the opposite.

questions.q: The road leading to Mr. Eze's farm was so NARROW that two vehicles could not pass through it at the same time. Choose the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals.
questions.e: Narrow means having a small width. Wide means having a large width, so it is the correct opposite of narrow in this context.
questions.p: Narrow mean say the road no big reach. Wide mean say e big well-well, so na im be the opposite.

questions.q: During the debate, Chief Obi's remarks were very HARSH, and many of the students felt discouraged afterwards. Choose the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals.
questions.e: Harsh means severe or unkind in manner. Gentle means mild and kind, which makes it the correct opposite in this sentence.
questions.p: Harsh mean say the talk hard or unkind. Gentle mean say e soft and kind, so na the correct opposite.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeyemi is known among her neighbours to be very FRUGAL with her household money. Choose the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals.
questions.e: Frugal means careful and economical when spending money. Wasteful means spending carelessly without control, which is its opposite.
questions.p: Frugal mean say person dey careful how e dey spend money. Wasteful mean say person dey spend anyhow, so na opposite.

questions.q: Chief Balogun was a TACITURN man who hardly spoke at village meetings, preferring to sit quietly and listen. Choose the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals.
questions.e: Taciturn describes someone who speaks very little. Talkative describes someone who speaks a lot, making it the true opposite. Silent and calm are close to taciturn in meaning, not opposite to it.
questions.p: Taciturn na person wey no dey talk plenty. Talkative na person wey dey always talk, so na im be the real opposite. Silent and calm resemble taciturn, dem no be opposite.

questions.q: Ngozi's answer to the question was so AMBIGUOUS that the examiner could not tell exactly what she meant. Choose the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals.
questions.e: Ambiguous means having more than one possible meaning or being unclear. Clear means easy to understand, which is the direct opposite. Confusing has a similar meaning to ambiguous, so it cannot be the opposite.
questions.p: Ambiguous mean say the answer no clear or e fit mean plenty things. Clear mean say e easy to understand, so na the opposite. Confusing resemble ambiguous, e no fit be the opposite.

questions.q: The chief invited all the elders to ______ the dispute between the two feuding families before it got out of hand.
questions.e: 'Settle' means to bring a disagreement to an end. The other options are wrong forms or change the meaning (unsettle means to disturb, resettle means to live in a new place again, and 'settlement' is a noun, not a verb).
questions.p: 'Settle' mean to make peace or end quarrel. The other words no fit work here because 'unsettle' mean to cause trouble, 'resettle' na to relocate, and 'settlement' na noun, e no fit follow 'to'.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The farmer's yam barn was completely EMPTY after the long famine.
questions.e: 'Bare' means having nothing inside, which matches 'empty'. 'Full' is the opposite, while 'heavy' and 'rotten' describe weight or condition, not emptiness.
questions.p: 'Bare' mean say nothing dey inside, na the same thing as 'empty'. 'Full' na opposite meaning, and 'heavy' or 'rotten' no talk about empty barn.

questions.q: Ngozi was so ______ that she forgot her own birthday last week.
questions.e: 'Forgetful' is the adjective that describes someone who easily forgets things, fitting the sentence. 'Memorable' means easy to remember, 'remembered' and 'forgetting' are wrong grammatical forms here.
questions.p: 'Forgetful' na adjective wey mean person wey dey quick forget. 'Memorable' mean say e easy to remember, and the other two no fit fit grammatically for that spot.

questions.q: The governor's campaign speech was full of ______ promises that nobody believed again.
questions.e: 'Empty promises' is a common expression meaning promises that will not be kept. 'Heavy', 'solid' and 'firm' do not collocate with 'promises' in this idiomatic sense.
questions.p: 'Empty promises' na common expression wey mean promise wey no go happen. 'Heavy', 'solid' and 'firm' no dey normally follow 'promises' like that.

questions.q: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The witness gave a very CREDIBLE account of the motor accident to the policemen.
questions.e: 'Credible' means believable, so its opposite is 'doubtful', which means something hard to believe. 'Believable', 'truthful' and 'honest' are all close in meaning to 'credible', not opposite.
questions.p: 'Credible' mean say na something wey person fit believe, so im opposite na 'doubtful' wey mean say e hard to believe. 'Believable', 'truthful' and 'honest' dey close to 'credible' meaning, no be opposite.

questions.q: Mr. Eze advised his son to ______ his studies seriously if he wants to pass his WAEC examination with good grades.
questions.e: The correct collocation is 'take something seriously'. 'Make', 'do' and 'have' do not combine correctly with 'seriously' in standard English usage.
questions.p: The correct combination na 'take something seriously'. 'Make', 'do' and 'have' no dey follow 'seriously' well for correct English.

questions.q: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: Despite the heavy rainfall, the farmers remained ______ in their resolve to finish planting before the big market day.
questions.e: 'Adamant' means firmly determined not to change one's mind, which fits the farmers' strong resolve despite the rain. 'Reluctant', 'indifferent' and 'hesitant' all suggest unwillingness or lack of interest, which contradicts the idea of staying determined.
questions.p: 'Adamant' mean say person don firmly decide and no go change mind, and dat one match the farmers wey still wan finish planting despite the rain. 'Reluctant', 'indifferent' and 'hesitant' mean say person no too wan do am, wey no match wit strong resolve.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Amina is married ___ a respected engineer who works in Abuja.
questions.e: The correct expression is 'married to someone'. 'Married with' or 'married by' are wrong in this context.
questions.p: The correct way to talk am na 'married to' person. 'Married with' or 'married by' no correct for this kain sentence.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ aware of the sudden change in the resumption date.
questions.e: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the noun nearer to it, which is 'teachers' (plural), so 'were' is correct.
questions.p: When you use 'neither...nor', the verb go agree with the noun wey close to am, wey be 'teachers' (plural). So 'were' na correct answer.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If Tunde ___ harder for the mock examination, he would have made better grades.
questions.e: This is a type 3 conditional sentence about an unreal past situation. It needs 'if + past perfect' followed by 'would have + past participle'.
questions.p: This na type 3 conditional, e dey talk about something wey no happen for past. E suppose be 'if + past perfect' and 'would have + past participle', so 'had studied' correct.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time the governor arrives at the stadium tomorrow, the students ___ the match.
questions.e: The action of finishing will be completed before another future action (the governor's arrival), so the future perfect tense 'will have finished' is needed.
questions.p: The finishing go don happen before another future action (governor reach), so we need future perfect tense, wey be 'will have finished'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The trader ___ shop was burnt down during the market fire has reopened her business at a new location.
questions.e: The sentence shows possession, that is, the shop belongs to the trader. The possessive relative pronoun 'whose' is used to show this relationship between people and things.
questions.p: The sentence dey show say the shop na the trader own, so we need possessive relative pronoun 'whose' to show that connection between person and the thing wey belong to am.

questions.q: Neither of the two prefects ___ absent yesterday.
questions.e: "Neither" is a singular pronoun, so it must be followed by a singular verb. The correct verb here is "was".
questions.p: "Neither" na singular word, so e dey take singular verb. Na "was" dey correct here.

questions.q: Each of the students in Mrs. Okafor's class ___ a copy of the novel.
questions.e: "Each" is singular, so the verb that follows it must also be singular. "Has" agrees correctly with "each".
questions.p: "Each" na singular pronoun, so di verb wey follow am must be singular too. "Has" dey match am well well.

questions.q: The jury ___ unanimous in its decision after deliberating for three hours.
questions.e: "Jury" is a collective noun, and in this sentence it is acting as one single unit (they agreed together). So it takes the singular verb "is".
questions.p: "Jury" na collective noun, and for dis sentence dem act as one body (dem agree together). So "is" dey correct as singular verb.

questions.q: Many a trader at Oyingbo market ___ lost goods during the flood.
questions.e: The phrase "many a" is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, even though the meaning is plural in sense. So "has" is correct.
questions.p: "Many a" dey always follow wit singular noun and singular verb, even though e dey mean plenty. So na "has" correct.

questions.q: Not only the headmaster but also the teachers ___ expected to attend the meeting.
questions.e: When two subjects are joined by "not only...but also", the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Since "teachers" (plural) is nearer, "are" is correct.
questions.p: When "not only...but also" join two subjects, di verb go agree wit di one wey near am. Since "teachers" (plural) near pass, "are" correct.

questions.q: The number of students who passed the WASSCE English paper ___ increased steadily over the past five years.
questions.e: "The number of" is treated as a singular subject because it refers to one total figure. Therefore the singular verb "has" is correct.
questions.p: "The number of" na singular subject because e dey talk about one total figure. So na singular verb "has" dey correct.

questions.q: A number of farmers in the community ___ affected by the recent drought.
questions.e: Unlike "the number of", the phrase "a number of" means "several" and is treated as plural. So the plural verb "were" is correct.
questions.p: Unlike "the number of", "a number of" mean "plenty" and e dey take plural verb. So "were" dey correct here.

questions.q: By the time the headmaster arrived, the students ___ the hall.
questions.e: Two past actions are compared, and the cleaning happened before the headmaster's arrival. The earlier past action takes the past perfect tense 'had cleaned'.
questions.p: Two past actions dey here, and di cleaning happen before headmaster come. Di action wey happen first must use past perfect 'had cleaned'.

questions.q: Chidinma ___ to the market every Saturday.
questions.e: The sentence describes a habitual action in the present, and the subject 'Chidinma' is third person singular, so the verb must agree and take 's' — 'goes'.
questions.p: Dis na habit wey Chidinma dey do every Saturday, and she na third person singular, so di verb must carry 's' — 'goes'.

questions.q: Since 2015, Mr. Okafor ___ English in this school.
questions.e: The word 'since' with a specific year shows an action that started in the past and continues till now, which requires the present perfect tense 'has taught'.
questions.p: Di word 'since' with year show say di action start since den dey continue till now, so e need present perfect 'has taught'.

questions.q: If the farmers ___ early, the crops would have yielded more.
questions.e: This is a third conditional sentence that talks about an unreal past situation. The 'if' clause must use the past perfect 'had planted' to match 'would have yielded' in the main clause.
questions.p: Dis na third conditional wey dey talk about something wey no happen for past. Di 'if' part must use 'had planted' to match 'would have yielded' for di main clause.

questions.q: Chidi is good ___ Mathematics, so his classmates often ask him for help.
questions.e: "Good at" is the correct collocation used when someone is skilled in a subject or activity.
questions.p: "Good at" na the correct one when you dey talk about person wey sabi one subject or work well.

questions.q: After a long meeting with the labour union, the government decided to CALL OFF the strike. What does the phrase in capitals mean?
questions.e: "Call off" means to cancel something that has been planned, such as a strike or a meeting.
questions.p: "Call off" mean to cancel something wey dem don plan, like strike or meeting.

questions.q: The trader was accused ___ selling expired rice to customers at the market.
questions.e: "Accused of" is the correct preposition that follows the verb "accuse" when referring to a wrongdoing.
questions.p: "Accused of" na the correct preposition wey dey follow "accuse" when you dey talk about wrong wey person do.

questions.q: Ngozi had to LOOK UP the meaning of the word "ubiquitous" because she did not understand it. What does the phrase in capitals mean here?
questions.e: In this sentence, "look up" means to search for information, especially in a reference book like a dictionary.
questions.p: For this sentence, "look up" mean to find information, especially inside book like dictionary.

questions.q: The Minister of Education will arrive ___ Abuja tomorrow for the national conference.
questions.e: "Arrive in" is used before the name of a country or a large city, while "arrive at" is used for smaller or specific places like a building or airport.
questions.p: "Arrive in" na the one wey dey follow country or big city name, but "arrive at" dey follow smaller place like building.

questions.q: Mrs. Okafor told her neighbour that she could no longer PUT UP WITH his loud music late at night. What does the phrase in capitals mean?
questions.e: "Put up with" is a phrasal verb that means to tolerate or endure something unpleasant.
questions.p: "Put up with" na phrasal verb wey mean to tolerate or endure something wey no sweet.

questions.q: The police commissioner ordered his men to LOOK INTO the case of the stolen motorcycle at Oshodi market. What does the phrase in capitals mean?
questions.e: "Look into" means to investigate or examine something carefully, which fits the context of the police checking a theft case.
questions.p: "Look into" mean to investigate or check something well, and e fit this matter of how police go check stolen motorcycle case.

questions.q: Mrs. Okafor told her son, 'Stop BEATING ABOUT THE BUSH and tell me exactly what happened at school.' What does the idiom in capitals mean?
o: Avoiding talking about the main point directly
questions.e: 'Beating about the bush' means avoiding the main subject instead of speaking directly about it. Mrs. Okafor wants her son to stop delaying and say the real matter.
questions.p: 'Beating about the bush' mean say person no wan talk the real matter straight. Mrs. Okafor want make her son stop to dey delay and talk wetin really happen.

questions.q: When Kemi heard that she had passed her WASSCE with distinctions, she said she was ON CLOUD NINE. What does the idiom in capitals mean?
questions.e: 'On cloud nine' is an idiom that means being extremely happy or overjoyed about something. Kemi felt this way because she passed with distinctions.
questions.p: 'On cloud nine' mean say person happy well well, like say the person dey fly for sky. Kemi feel like that because she pass her WASSCE well.

questions.q: Although Ada and Efe used to be close friends, they are now ______ because of a disagreement over their late father's land.
questions.e: 'At daggers drawn' means to be in a state of open hostility or disagreement with someone. The other options all describe closeness or similarity, which does not fit the quarrel described.
questions.p: 'At daggers drawn' mean say two people dey fight or no dey agree at all. The other options mean say people close well well, so dem no fit fit this story of quarrel.

questions.q: During a board meeting at a Lagos firm, the chairman accidentally mentioned the secret plan to merge two companies before the official announcement was made. Which idiom best describes what the chairman did?
o: He turned over a new leaf
He let the cat out of the bag
questions.e: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret, usually by accident. This fits the chairman revealing the merger plan before it was officially announced.
questions.p: 'Let the cat out of the bag' mean say person don expose secret, sometimes na mistake. Na so the chairman talk the merger matter before dem announce am.

questions.q: Three of the following idioms mean 'to work very hard', while one has a different meaning. Which one is the odd one out?
questions.e: 'Sit on the fence' means to remain neutral or undecided about an issue, not to work hard. The other three idioms all describe putting in great effort or working very hard.
questions.p: 'Sit on the fence' mean say person no wan choose side, e no dey about hard work. The other three idioms dey talk about person wey dey work hard well well.

questions.q: After failing Woodwork badly in her mock examination, Ngozi decided to TURN OVER A NEW LEAF. What does the idiom in capitals mean?
o: To seek transfer to another school
To give up completely on her studies
To begin to behave or work in a better way
questions.e: 'Turn over a new leaf' means to change one's behaviour for the better, often after a mistake or failure. Ngozi is choosing to improve after her poor result.
questions.p: 'Turn over a new leaf' mean say person don decide to change for better, especially after mistake. Na so Ngozi wan improve after she fail her mock.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "It was not until Ngozi got to Lagos that she realized she had forgotten her certificates at home."
o: Ngozi realized she had forgotten her certificates before she left for Lagos.
Ngozi did not realize she had forgotten her certificates until she arrived in Lagos.
Ngozi never forgot her certificates at home.
Ngozi forgot her certificates only after she got to Lagos.
questions.e: The phrase 'not until... that' shows the realization only happened when Ngozi got to Lagos, not before. So she discovered her mistake after arriving, not before leaving.
questions.p: Di phrase 'not until... that' mean say na when Ngozi reach Lagos she come notice say she forget her certificates. E no be say she don already know before she travel.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "Chidi is yet to finish his assignment."
o: Chidi refused to do his assignment.
Chidi has finished his assignment already.
Chidi will never finish his assignment.
Chidi has not finished his assignment.
questions.e: 'Yet to finish' means the action has not happened at the time of speaking. It simply means Chidi has not completed the assignment, with no suggestion of refusal or permanence.
questions.p: 'Yet to finish' mean say di work never complete as dem dey talk am. E just mean Chidi never finish di assignment, no be say e refuse to do am.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "Mr. Okafor is not unaware of the problems facing his business."
o: Mr. Okafor does not know about the problems facing his business.
Mr. Okafor is confused about his business problems.
Mr. Okafor is aware of the problems facing his business.
Mr. Okafor has refused to solve the problems facing his business.
questions.e: The sentence uses a double negative: 'not' + 'unaware'. Two negatives cancel out to give a positive meaning, so Mr. Okafor is indeed aware of the problems.
questions.p: Dis sentence get double negative: 'not' and 'unaware'. Wen you join two negative togeda, e turn to positive, so e mean Mr. Okafor sabi di problems well well.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "Hardly had the teacher entered the class when the students began to make noise."
o: The students began making noise soon after the teacher entered the class.
The students stopped making noise when the teacher entered.
The students made noise before the teacher entered the class.
The teacher made noise before entering the class.
questions.e: 'Hardly... when' shows that two actions happened almost at the same time, with the second one (noise-making) following immediately after the first (teacher entering). So the noise started right after the teacher came in.
questions.p: 'Hardly... when' dey show say two things happen almost same time, but di noise start immediately after teacher enter class. So di noise no come before, e come after small time.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "Had Musa studied harder, he would have passed the examination."
o: Musa studied hard but still failed the examination.
Musa did not study hard, so he failed the examination.
Musa will study harder next time to pass.
Musa studied hard and passed the examination.
questions.e: This is a conditional sentence (third conditional) showing an unreal past situation. Since Musa did not study harder, the implied result is that he failed the examination.
questions.p: Dis na conditional sentence wey dey show something wey no happen for di past. Since Musa no study hard, e mean say e fail di exam.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "The chief's speech was nothing but empty promises."
o: The chief's speech was full of useful ideas.
The chief refused to make any promises in his speech.
The chief's speech was very short.
The chief's speech contained only promises that will not be fulfilled.
questions.e: 'Nothing but' means 'only'. 'Empty promises' means promises with no real intention of being kept. So the speech was made up only of promises that will likely not be fulfilled.
questions.p: 'Nothing but' mean 'only'. 'Empty promises' mean promises wey no get real intention to fulfil. So di whole speech na just promises wey no go happen.

questions.q: What is the meaning of this sentence? "Were it not for the timely intervention of the police, the fight between the two communities would have escalated."
o: The police did not intervene, so the fight escalated.
The police's intervention came too late to stop the fight.
The fight escalated despite the police's intervention.
The police intervened on time and this prevented the fight from escalating.
questions.e: This is a conditional sentence showing a situation that did not happen because something else prevented it. The police did intervene on time, and because of that timely action, the fight did not get worse.
questions.p: Dis na conditional sentence wey dey show say one thing no happen because another thing stop am. Police intervene on time, na im make di fight no escalate.

questions.q: Ngozi and ___ are planning to visit Kano next week.
questions.e: The pronoun is the subject of the verb 'are planning', so the subject form 'I' is correct. 'Me' is an object pronoun, 'myself' is reflexive, and 'mine' shows possession, none of which fit here.
questions.p: The pronoun na subject for the verb 'are planning', so na 'I' dey correct. 'Me' na object pronoun, 'myself' na reflexive, 'mine' na possession, dem no fit fit here.

questions.q: Emeka is the best footballer in our school, ___?
questions.e: The main statement is positive and uses the verb 'is', so the tag must be negative and use the same auxiliary verb 'is' with the matching pronoun 'he'. 'Isn't he' is the correct tag.
questions.p: The main statement na positive and e dey use 'is', so the tag suppose negative and use the same 'is' with 'he'. 'Isn't he' na the correct tag.

questions.q: The farmers have not harvested their yams, ___?
questions.e: Since the statement is negative ('have not harvested'), the tag must be positive, using the same auxiliary verb 'have' and the pronoun 'they'. So 'have they' is correct.
questions.p: Since the statement negative ('have not harvested'), the tag suppose positive, with the same 'have' and pronoun 'they'. So 'have they' na the correct one.

questions.q: There is ___ sugar left in the tin, so we cannot make more tea.
questions.e: 'Sugar' is an uncountable noun, so 'few' and 'a few' (used for countable nouns) are wrong. 'Little' shows almost none is left, which matches the reason given for not making more tea.
questions.p: 'Sugar' na uncountable noun, so 'few' and 'a few' (wey dey work for countable noun) no fit work. 'Little' show say almost nothing remain, and e match why dem no fit make more tea.

questions.q: Bola looked at ___ in the mirror before leaving for the party.
questions.e: Since Bola is both the person doing the looking and the one being looked at, a reflexive pronoun is needed. 'Herself' correctly shows the action reflects back on the subject.
questions.p: Since na Bola dey look and na im body she dey look, reflexive pronoun dey needed. 'Herself' show well well say the action dey return back to the subject.

questions.q: Let's finish this assignment before the teacher returns, ___?
questions.e: Sentences beginning with 'Let's' (a suggestion) always take the special tag 'shall we', regardless of whether the sentence is positive or negative. This is a fixed exception in English grammar.
questions.p: Any sentence wey start with 'Let's' (as suggestion) always dey take the special tag 'shall we', no matter if e positive or negative. Na fixed exception for English grammar.

questions.q: In banking, the word in capitals is used in this sentence: 'Before the loan was approved, the bank manager asked Mrs. Adaeze to provide some COLLATERAL.' The word in capitals means nearest to:
questions.e: Collateral is an asset (like land or a car) that a borrower offers to a bank as security for a loan. If the borrower fails to repay, the bank can sell the collateral.
questions.p: Collateral na property wey person give bank as guarantee before dem go gree give am loan. If person no pay back, bank fit sell the property.

questions.q: In legal register, the person who brings a civil case to court against another person is called the:
questions.e: The plaintiff is the one who starts a civil lawsuit, while the defendant is the person being sued. A magistrate judges the case, and a witness gives testimony.
questions.p: Plaintiff na the person wey carry case go court against another person. Defendant na the one wey dem sue, magistrate na judge, witness na the one wey go testify.

questions.q: A doctor tells a patient's family, 'The PROGNOSIS for her recovery is good.' The word in capitals is nearest in meaning to:
o: forecast about the likely course of a disease
questions.e: Prognosis refers to a doctor's prediction of how a disease or illness is likely to develop or end, not a medical record or test result.
questions.p: Prognosis na doctor own prediction of how the sickness go turn out, e no be patient history or test result.

questions.q: A bank in Lagos holds large sums in government bonds that take months to sell, while another bank keeps most of its funds in cash and short-term treasury bills that can be accessed within days. In banking terms, the second bank has higher:
questions.e: Liquidity means how quickly an asset can be turned into cash to meet urgent obligations. The second bank can access cash faster, so it has higher liquidity, while solvency relates to total assets exceeding liabilities, not speed of conversion.
questions.p: Liquidity na how quick asset fit turn to cash. The second bank get money wey e fit use sharp sharp, so im liquidity high pass. Solvency na different thing, e be say your asset pass your debt.

questions.q: After the trial, the judge said, 'The court hereby grants an ACQUITTAL to the accused.' The word in capitals means:
questions.e: An acquittal means the court has found the accused person not guilty and he is set free. It is the opposite of a conviction or sentencing.
questions.p: Acquittal mean say court don declare say the person no guilty, so dem go free am. Na opposite of when dem convict or sentence person.

questions.q: Read the passage and answer the question that follows: During the inter-house sports competition at Government Secondary School, Kaduna, Tunde suffered a slight injury in the 100-metre race. The coach quickly brought in another athlete to take his place so that the Blue House team would not lose vital points. What is the athlete who replaces Tunde called in sports register?
questions.e: A substitute is a player who comes in to replace another player during a competition, which is exactly what happened to Tunde in the passage.
questions.p: Substitute na the player wey enter replace another player for competition, na wetin happen to Tunde for the passage.

questions.q: In the sentence: 'Tunde answered the difficult question SURPRISINGLY well during the interview,' what word class is the word in capitals?
questions.e: The word 'surprisingly' describes the adverb 'well', telling us how well he answered. A word that modifies another adverb (or adjective/verb) is an adverb.
questions.p: 'Surprisingly' dey describe the word 'well', e dey show how e take answer well. Word wey dey modify another adverb na adverb.

questions.q: Choose the correct word class of the word in capitals: 'Before the exam started, Blessing QUIETLY arranged her pens and pencils on the desk.'
questions.e: 'Quietly' tells us how Blessing arranged her items, so it modifies the verb 'arranged'. Words that modify verbs by showing manner are adverbs.
questions.p: 'Quietly' dey show how Blessing arrange her things, so e dey modify the verb 'arranged'. Word wey dey show manner for verb na adverb.

questions.q: Which word class is the word in capitals? 'The goat jumped OVER the fence and ran into the bush.'
questions.e: 'Over' shows the relationship between 'jumped' and 'the fence', indicating position or movement. Words that link a noun to another part of a sentence to show place, time or direction are prepositions.
questions.p: 'Over' dey show how 'jumped' connect to 'the fence', e dey show direction. Word wey dey link noun to show place or direction na preposition.

questions.q: Study this sentence carefully: 'The tired market woman carrying a heavy basket of pepper is waiting for a taxi.' Which group of words is a noun phrase?
o: The tired market woman carrying a heavy basket of pepper
carrying a heavy basket of pepper
questions.e: A noun phrase is built around a noun as its head word, with other words describing it. 'The tired market woman carrying a heavy basket of pepper' has 'woman' as its head noun, and it functions as the subject of the sentence.
questions.p: Noun phrase na group of words wey get noun as the main word, with other words wey dey describe am. 'The tired market woman carrying a heavy basket of pepper' get 'woman' as the main noun, and e be the subject.

questions.q: In the sentence: 'Because the rain refused to stop, the traders at Oja-Oba market packed up their goods early,' which part is the subordinate (dependent) clause?
o: Because the rain refused to stop
questions.e: A subordinate clause has a subject and verb but cannot stand alone as a complete sentence; it depends on another clause for full meaning. 'Because the rain refused to stop' begins with the subordinating conjunction 'because' and needs the main clause to make complete sense.
questions.p: Subordinate clause get subject and verb but e no fit stand alone as full sentence; e need the main clause before e go complete. 'Because the rain refused to stop' start with 'because' and e need the main clause to complete the meaning.

questions.q:
Consider these four groups of words:
I. running fast to catch the bus
II. because he ran fast
III. the fast runner
IV. in the early morning
Which one of these is a CLAUSE rather than a phrase?
questions.e: A clause must contain a subject and a finite verb. Only 'because he ran fast' has the subject 'he' and the verb 'ran', while the other three groups lack a subject-verb pair and are therefore phrases.
questions.p: Clause must get subject and verb wey complete. Na only 'because he ran fast' get subject 'he' and verb 'ran', the other three no get subject-verb pair, so na phrase dem be.

questions.q: Which of the following options contains the correctly spelled word?
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'ACCOMMODATE', with double 'c' and double 'm'. The other options are common misspellings of this word.
questions.p: The correct spelling na 'ACCOMMODATE', e get double 'c' and double 'm'. The rest na how people dey spell am wrong anyhow.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that is correctly punctuated.
o: "Its time for the match," said Emeka.
"It's time for the match," said Emeka.
"Its' time for the match," said Emeka.
"It's time for the match", said Emeka.
questions.e: 'It's' is the correct contraction of 'it is', and the comma that ends the quoted speech must be placed inside the quotation marks. The other options either misuse the apostrophe or place the comma wrongly.
questions.p: 'It's' na correct short form for 'it is', and the comma wey dey close the speech suppose dey inside the quotation marks. The other options don mismanage the apostrophe or comma.

questions.q: From the options below, choose the word that is correctly spelled.
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'NECESSARY', with one 'c' and double 's'. A common memory trick is: one collar (c), two sleeves (ss).
questions.p: Correct spelling na 'NECESSARY', na one 'c' and double 's'. Remember am as one collar (c), two sleeves (ss).

questions.q: Which of the following words is WRONGLY spelled?
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'privilege', not 'priviledge'; there is no 'd' before the 'ge'. The other three words are correctly spelled, though they often trick students because of double letters.
questions.p: Correct spelling na 'privilege', no 'd' before 'ge'. The remaining three words dem spell correctly, but students dey mistake dem sake of the double letters.

questions.q:
From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the word in capitals.
CAT
questions.e: The word in capitals, CAT, has the short vowel sound /æ/ as in 'bag'. BACK also has /æ/. CAKE and CARE have the diphthong /eɪ/ and /eə/, while CAR has the long vowel /ɑː/.
questions.p: The word for capitals, CAT, get the short sound /æ/ like for 'bag'. BACK get the same /æ/ sound. CAKE and CARE get different diphthong sounds, CAR get long /ɑː/ sound.

questions.q:
From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the word in capitals.
FEAST
questions.e: FEAST has the long vowel sound /i:/. BEACH also has /i:/. BREAD has /e/, GREAT has /eɪ/, and BEAR has /eə/.
questions.p: FEAST get long /i:/ sound. BEACH too get /i:/. BREAD get /e/, GREAT get /eɪ/, BEAR get /eə/, na why dem no match.

questions.q:
From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the word in capitals.
SUIT
questions.e: SUIT is pronounced with the long vowel /u:/ as in 'moon'. BOOT shares this sound. FOOT has the short /ʊ/, OUT has the diphthong /aʊ/, and BUT has /ʌ/.
questions.p: SUIT get long /u:/ sound like for 'moon'. BOOT get the same one. FOOT na short /ʊ/, OUT na /aʊ/, BUT na /ʌ/, so dem no match.

questions.q: In each of the words PEAK, SPEAK, LEAK and BREAK, the vowel sound is the same except in one word. From the options lettered A to D, identify the word with the different vowel sound.
questions.e: PEAK, SPEAK and LEAK all have the long vowel /i:/. BREAK is pronounced with the diphthong /eɪ/, making it the odd one out, even though it looks spelt like the others.
questions.p: PEAK, SPEAK and LEAK all get /i:/ sound. BREAK na /eɪ/ sound, e be the different one even though e resemble the others for spelling.

questions.q: In each of the words COW, HOW, NOW and BOY, the vowel sound is the same except in one word. From the options lettered A to D, identify the word with the different vowel sound.
questions.e: COW, HOW and NOW all contain the diphthong /aʊ/. BOY contains a different diphthong, /ɔɪ/, so it does not share the same vowel sound as the other three.
questions.p: COW, HOW and NOW all get /aʊ/ sound. BOY get different diphthong /ɔɪ/, so e no match the other three.

questions.q:
From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the word in capitals.
PUT
questions.e: PUT is pronounced with the short vowel /ʊ/ as in 'book'. PUSH has the same /ʊ/ sound. PUB and PUN have /ʌ/, while PURE has a different glide sound /jʊə/.
questions.p: PUT get short /ʊ/ sound like for 'book'. PUSH get the same /ʊ/. PUB and PUN na /ʌ/, PURE na different /jʊə/ sound.

questions.q:
From the options lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same final vowel sound as the word in capitals.
TEACHER
questions.e: In Received Pronunciation, TEACHER ends with the unstressed schwa sound /ə/. MIRROR also ends with /ə/. CHAIR, HAIR and CARE all end with the diphthong /eə/, which is a different sound.
questions.p: For correct British pronunciation, TEACHER dey end with weak schwa sound /ə/. MIRROR too dey end with /ə/. CHAIR, HAIR and CARE dey end with /eə/ sound, na different one.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word whose underlined consonant sound is different from the others. All the words begin with the letters 'CH'.
A. CHAIR
B. CHEMIST
C. CHURCH
D. CHEESE
questions.e: CHAIR, CHURCH and CHEESE all begin with the sound /tʃ/ as in 'chop'. CHEMIST begins with the sound /k/ instead. So CHEMIST is the odd one out.
questions.p: CHAIR, CHURCH and CHEESE all dey start with /tʃ/ sound like 'chop'. But CHEMIST dey start with /k/ sound. So na CHEMIST be the odd one.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that begins with a consonant cluster.
A. SPLASH
B. TABLE
C. WATER
D. APPLE
questions.e: SPLASH begins with three consonant sounds together, /spl/, which is a consonant cluster. TABLE, WATER and APPLE do not start with clustered consonant sounds.
questions.p: SPLASH dey start with /spl/ wey be three consonant sounds join together, na so consonant cluster dey be. TABLE, WATER and APPLE no get that kind start.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has a silent consonant.
A. CASTLE
B. CAMEL
C. CARROT
D. CABBAGE
questions.e: In CASTLE, the letter 't' is silent, so it is pronounced /ˈkɑːsəl/. The other words have all their consonants pronounced.
questions.p: For CASTLE, the 't' no dey pronounce, dem dey call am /ˈkɑːsəl/. The other words dey pronounce all their consonants well well.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that contains the consonant sound /θ/ as heard in 'think'.
A. THESE
B. MOTHER
C. THIRD
D. FATHER
questions.e: THIRD is pronounced with the voiceless sound /θ/, just like 'think'. THESE, MOTHER and FATHER all contain the voiced sound /ð/ instead.
questions.p: THIRD dey use the voiceless /θ/ sound, the same way as 'think'. THESE, MOTHER and FATHER dey use /ð/ sound wey be voiced one.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that ends with a consonant cluster.
A. TEXT
B. TRAY
C. TABLE
D. TOMATO
questions.e: TEXT ends with the sounds /kst/, which is a cluster of three consonant sounds together. TRAY, TABLE and TOMATO do not end with clustered consonant sounds.
questions.p: TEXT dey end with /kst/, wey be three consonant sounds join finish. TRAY, TABLE and TOMATO no get that kind ending.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that ends with the same consonant sound as the word in capitals.
BRIDGE
A. REACH
B. JUDGE
C. WATCH
D. BENCH
questions.e: BRIDGE ends with the voiced sound /dʒ/. JUDGE also ends with /dʒ/. REACH, WATCH and BENCH all end with the voiceless sound /tʃ/ instead.
questions.p: BRIDGE dey end with /dʒ/ sound wey be voiced. JUDGE too dey end with /dʒ/. REACH, WATCH and BENCH dey end with /tʃ/ wey no be voiced.

questions.q:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that does NOT begin with a three-consonant cluster.
A. STRAY
B. SPRAY
C. STOP
D. SCREAM
questions.e: STRAY begins with /str/, SPRAY with /spr/, and SCREAM with /skr/, each having three consonant sounds together. STOP only begins with /st/, which is a two-consonant cluster, so it does not fit the three-consonant pattern.
questions.p: STRAY dey start with /str/, SPRAY with /spr/, SCREAM with /skr/, all na three consonant sounds join together. STOP na only /st/, na two consonant sounds, e no match the three-consonant pattern.

questions.q: Which syllable is stressed in the word in capitals: EXPORT (used as a noun meaning goods sent to another country)?
questions.e: As a noun, EXPORT is stressed on the first syllable: EX-port. When it is used as a verb (to export goods), the stress moves to the second syllable, ex-PORT.
questions.p: As noun, EXPORT dey stress for first syllable: EX-port. If e be verb (to export something), na second syllable dem go stress: ex-PORT.

questions.q: Chidi said, 'The soldiers plan to REBEL against the unjust government.' In the word REBEL as used in this sentence (a verb meaning to rise up against authority), which syllable is stressed?
o: Stress depends on the speaker's accent
questions.e: REBEL used as a verb is stressed on the second syllable: re-BEL. The noun form, meaning a person who resists authority, is stressed on the first syllable: REB-el.
questions.p: As verb, REBEL dey stress for second syllable: re-BEL. But as noun (person wey dey fight authority), na first syllable dem go stress: REB-el.

questions.q:
Which of the following words has its main stress on a different syllable from the other three?
A. HOSPITAL
B. ELEPHANT
C. UMBRELLA
D. CALENDAR
questions.e: HOSPITAL, ELEPHANT and CALENDAR are all stressed on the first syllable (HOS-pi-tal, EL-e-phant, CAL-en-dar). UMBRELLA is different because it is stressed on the second syllable: um-BREL-la.
questions.p: HOSPITAL, ELEPHANT and CALENDAR dem all dey stress for first syllable. But UMBRELLA no be like dat; na second syllable dem dey stress: um-BREL-la.

questions.q: The words PHOTOGRAPH, PHOTOGRAPHY and PHOTOGRAPHIC share the same root but their stress changes with the suffix added. In the word PHOTOGRAPHY, which syllable carries the main stress?
questions.e: PHOTOGRAPH is stressed on the first syllable (PHO-to-graph), but adding '-y' shifts the stress to the second syllable in PHOTOGRAPHY: pho-TOG-ra-phy. This shows how a suffix can move the stress in a word.
questions.p: PHOTOGRAPH dey stress for first syllable (PHO-to-graph), but as dem add '-y' make am PHOTOGRAPHY, the stress shift go second syllable: pho-TOG-ra-phy. Na so suffix fit change where stress dey.

questions.q: Which syllable is stressed in the word in capitals: BLACKBOARD (the writing board used by teachers in a classroom)?
questions.e: BLACKBOARD is a compound noun, and compound nouns in English are usually stressed on the first part: BLACK-board. This is different from a simple phrase like 'a black board,' where both words can carry stress.
questions.p: BLACKBOARD na compound noun, and compound noun dem dey normally stress for the first part: BLACK-board. E different from ordinary phrase like 'a black board' where both words fit get stress.

questions.q: In the word EDUCATION, which syllable carries the main stress?
questions.e: EDUCATION has four syllables: ed-u-CA-tion. Words ending in '-tion' are usually stressed on the syllable just before the ending, which here is 'ca', making the third syllable the stressed one.
questions.p: EDUCATION get four syllables: ed-u-CA-tion. Words wey dey end for '-tion' dey normally stress the syllable before the ending, so na third syllable 'ca' carry the stress.

questions.q:
In which of the following sentences is the word RECORD stressed on the second syllable?
A. Ngozi broke the world RECORD for the 100-metre race.
B. The clerk had to RECORD all the names in the register.
C. Please keep a RECORD of your daily expenses.
D. The teacher kept an attendance RECORD for the term.
o: The clerk had to RECORD all the names in the register.
Ngozi broke the world RECORD for the 100-metre race.
The teacher kept an attendance RECORD for the term.
Please keep a RECORD of your daily expenses.
questions.e: RECORD used as a verb (meaning to write something down) is stressed on the second syllable: re-CORD, as in sentence B. In the other sentences, RECORD is used as a noun, stressed on the first syllable: REC-ord.
questions.p: RECORD wey be verb (meaning to write something down) dey stress for second syllable: re-CORD, as e dey for sentence B. For the other sentences, RECORD na noun, so na first syllable dem dey stress: REC-ord.

questions.q: In spoken English, emphatic stress is mainly used to
o: show that a sentence is a question
give special importance to a particular word in a sentence
questions.e: Emphatic stress means saying one word louder or stronger than the others to highlight it or show it is important. It is not about length, questions, or lists.
questions.p: Emphatic stress na when you talk one word louder pass di oda ones so dat e go show say dat word important. E no concern how long word be, or question, or list.

questions.q: Which of these sentences would normally be spoken with a RISING intonation from start to end?
questions.e: Yes/No questions like 'Did Chidinma travel to Lagos?' are said with a rising tune because the answer is simply yes or no. The other options are Wh- questions, which take a falling tune.
questions.p: Yes or No question like 'Did Chidinma travel to Lagos?' dey use rising tune because di answer na just yes or no. Di oda ones na Wh- questions wey dey take falling tune.

questions.q: Mr Eze said that Amina bought the bag, but in fact it was Kemi who bought the bag. If Funke wants to correct Mr Eze by emphasising the right person, which word should she stress?
questions.e: The mistake is about who did the buying, not what was bought or the action itself. So the word 'KEMI' must carry the emphatic stress to correct the wrong information.
questions.p: Di mistake na about who buy di bag, e no concern wetin dem buy or di action. So na 'KEMI' suppose carry di stress to correct di wrong tin wey Mr Eze talk.

questions.q: Adaeze asks her brother, 'You will attend the wedding, won't you?' and says the tag 'won't you' with a FALLING tone. What does this falling tone suggest?
o: Adaeze is certain and only wants her brother to confirm
Adaeze is asking a plain yes/no question
Adaeze is unsure and is genuinely asking a question
Adaeze is reading out a list of items
questions.e: A falling tone on a tag question shows the speaker already believes the statement is true and just wants agreement. A rising tone would instead show real doubt.
questions.p: When tag question get falling tone, e mean say di speaker don already believe say di tin na true, e just wan make di oda person agree. If e be rising tone, e go show say di speaker dey really doubt.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about question intonation is CORRECT?
o: Wh- questions are usually said with a rising tone
Yes/No questions are usually said with a falling tone
All questions must end with a rising tone
Wh- questions are usually said with a falling tone
questions.e: Questions that begin with Wh- words (who, what, where, why, how) are normally said with a falling tone, while Yes/No questions take a rising tone. So option D is the correct rule.
questions.p: Questions wey start with Wh- words (who, wetin, where, why, how) dey take falling tone, while Yes/No questions dey take rising tone. So option D na di correct rule.

questions.q: Musa is reading out a shopping list: 'I bought rice, beans, garri and oil.' Which intonation pattern is the correct way to say this list?
o: Rising tone on each item except 'oil', which falls
Rising tone on every item, including 'oil'
Falling tone on each item except 'oil', which rises
Falling tone on every item, including 'oil'
questions.e: In a list, each item before the last one is said with a rising tone to show more items are coming, while the final item takes a falling tone to show the list has ended.
questions.p: For list, every item before di last one dey take rising tone to show say more items dey come, while di last item dey take falling tone to show say di list don finish.

questions.q: A man says, 'I did not say he stole the money.' If he wants to make it clear that SOMEONE ELSE said it, and not him, which word in the sentence should carry the emphatic stress?
questions.e: To show that another person, not the speaker, made the statement, the pronoun 'I' must be stressed. Stressing other words like 'stole' would instead question whether the money was actually stolen.
questions.p: To show say na anoda person talk am, no be di speaker, dem must stress di word 'I'. If dem stress 'stole' instead, e go mean say dem dey doubt whether dem actually steal di money.

questions.q: Which of the following words rhymes with the word in capitals: CHAIR?
questions.e: FAIR is pronounced /feə/, which has the same ending sound as CHAIR /tʃeə/. The other words end with different vowel sounds.
questions.p: FAIR dey sound /feə/ and e match CHAIR /tʃeə/ for the back part. The other words no get that same sound.

questions.q: Choose the word that is a homophone of the word in capitals: SEA.
questions.e: SEA and SEE are pronounced exactly the same way, /siː/, but have different spellings and meanings. The other options sound different from SEA.
questions.p: SEA and SEE get the same sound /siː/ but dem no mean the same thing. The other words sound different.

questions.q: Which of the following words rhymes with the word in capitals: FEAR?
questions.e: FEAR /fɪə/ and YEAR /jɪə/ share the same ending sound. BEAR and FAIR end in /eə/, while FUR ends in a totally different sound.
questions.p: FEAR and YEAR get the same back sound /ɪə/. BEAR and FAIR get different sound /eə/, and FUR no even close at all.

questions.q: Choose the word that is a homophone of the word in capitals: WEAK.
questions.e: WEAK and WEEK are both pronounced /wiːk/, even though one refers to strength and the other to a period of seven days. The other options have different vowel sounds.
questions.p: WEAK and WEEK dey sound the same /wiːk/, but one mean say person no strong, the other one mean seven days. The other words no sound like am.

questions.q: Which of the following words rhymes with the word in capitals: BOUGHT?
questions.e: BOUGHT /bɔːt/ and TAUGHT /tɔːt/ both end with the same long vowel and consonant sound. BOAT, BOUT and BOUGH all have different vowel sounds from BOUGHT.
questions.p: BOUGHT and TAUGHT get the same ending sound /ɔːt/. BOAT, BOUT and BOUGH no get that kain sound.

questions.q: Three of the following words rhyme with one another while one does not. Which word does NOT rhyme with the others: TOUGH, ROUGH, ENOUGH, COUGH?
questions.e: TOUGH, ROUGH and ENOUGH are all pronounced with the /ʌf/ sound at the end, but COUGH is pronounced with /ɒf/, which is a different vowel sound. This shows that 'ough' spelling does not always give the same sound in English.
questions.p: TOUGH, ROUGH and ENOUGH dey end with /ʌf/ sound, but COUGH dey end with /ɒf/ which be different vowel. Na so 'ough' spelling fit sound different-different for English.

questions.q: Chief Nduka was a wise ruler who was loved by his people. Choose the correct homophone to complete the sentence: 'The king began his ___ at a young age, and his people respected him greatly.'
questions.e: REIGN means the period a king or queen rules, which fits the sentence about the king's rule. RAIN refers to water falling from the sky, REIN is used to control a horse, and these are all homophones of REIGN but wrong in meaning here.
questions.p: REIGN mean the time wey king or queen dey rule, and na im fit the sentence well. RAIN na water wey dey fall from sky, REIN na the thing wey dem dey use control horse; all of dem sound like REIGN but dem no fit the meaning here.

questions.q:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows:

Adaeze, a young graduate from Nnewi, returned to her village determined to change local farming methods. While most elders still relied on crude tools and age-old superstitions, she introduced simple irrigation and organic fertilizers. At first, the villagers mocked her, calling her efforts a WASTE of time. However, after her maize farm yielded three times more than others, many began to seek her advice. Adaeze's quiet confidence and patience eventually earned her the respect she had initially been denied. Her story became a lesson to the community that KNOWLEDGE, not age alone, could bring progress.

What was Adaeze's occupation or background as described in the passage?
o: a young graduate who introduced new farming methods
questions.e: The passage clearly states that Adaeze was a young graduate who returned to her village and introduced new farming methods like irrigation and organic fertilizers.
questions.p: Di passage talk am clear sey Adaeze na young graduate wey come back im village come bring new farming method like irrigation and organic fertilizer.
